question: Should existing GitHub-backed skills with over-40-character stored display names be grandfathered like hosted skills, or intentionally shortened on their next sync?
rationale: The PR chooses a compatibility-sensitive policy for stored catalog metadata, and automation should not decide whether existing GitHub-backed names are preserved or migrated.

options.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed legacy names
options.body: Preserve unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names and enforce the limit only for new or renamed GitHub-backed entries.

options.title: Accept sync-time shortening
options.body: Allow existing GitHub-backed over-limit names to be shortened on next sync, but document that migration and add upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause display-name policy
options.body: Keep this PR open until maintainers choose both the public maximum length and legacy handling for hosted and GitHub-backed skills.

recommendation.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed legacy names
recommendation.body: Preserve unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names and enforce the limit only for new or renamed GitHub-backed entries.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the strongest current-main history for the GitHub-backed sync and shared publish paths affected by the policy decision.
